name: Rotor Abyss
description: Rotor Abyss is a cold, deep ocean world where enormous whirlpools form and dissipate in regular cycles, each vortex spanning hundreds of kilometers and drilling down to the planet's geothermal seabed. The surface is a slate-gray expanse under perpetual overcast skies, broken only by the spiraling white foam of the great rotors and the occasional volcanic seamount that briefly breaches the waves. The planet's dense atmosphere traps moisture in layered cloud systems that rotate in the same direction as the whirlpools below.

The sensation aboard a vessel on Rotor Abyss is one of constant, slow rotation, as even calm waters carry a gentle circular current. The air is cold and heavy, tasting of salt and sulfur from the geothermal vents, and the low-frequency rumble of the whirlpools creates a subsonic vibration that can be felt in the chest. Visibility is limited by perpetual mist, and the boundary between sea and sky blurs into a featureless gray that disorients the unwary.

The whirlpools are driven by an interaction between geothermal heat and anomalous gravity wells scattered across the seabed, points where gravitational force intensifies without any corresponding mass concentration. These gravity wells appear and disappear on cycles ranging from days to decades, and their migration patterns have never been successfully predicted. Microbial communities thrive in the warm water around the vents, forming spiraling biofilm structures that rotate in miniature echo of the great whirlpools above.

Helium-3 concentrations in Rotor Abyss's atmosphere make it a valuable fuel harvesting location, but the unpredictable gravity wells make sustained orbital operations hazardous. Ships caught in the whirlpools' outer reaches can escape with sufficient thrust, but the inner rotations generate forces that have crushed reinforced hulls. The gravity wells' origin remains one of the sector's enduring mysteries, and the prevailing theory, that they are artifacts of some ancient technology embedded in the planet's core, has yet to be proven or disproven.
